To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

we developed a fast and secure access control technology solution that uses a combination of radio-frequency identification (RFID), face recognition (FR), and a unique tri-band camera to provide a positive identification of the driver and vehicle in motion at a gate.
the FACTS solution combines RFID tags with FRS to reduce the one-to-many problem of FRS to a one-to-one problem for facial verification (positive ID) of motorists at a gated entrance.

we have developed a fast and convenient access control system that uses a one-to-one face match for fast, reliable, and positive identification of motorists entering the gates of secured parking lots, manufacturing plants, etc., and is dynamic, secure and hands-free.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development and implementation of a fast access control solution for a one-to-many ACS application.
the development of a biometric-based access-control system for large-scale applications that is dynamic, positive, and fast.
the development of a new technology for fast, secure access control of large numbers of people in a short time.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
FACTS is a reliable and secure solution for positive ID in a one-to-one application, and a practical and cost-effective solution for a one-to-many access control problem.
the FACTS system is a reliable, positive, dynamic, and secure access control system for large numbers of people.
the FACTS system provides fast access control to a large number of motorists in a short time with positive ID verification.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have developed a new FRS that can reliably locate and recognize a face from a distance in a dynamic environment, such as a gate entry, and in less than 1 s.
the FACTS solution is an effective and efficient solution that can be used for a wide variety of access control applications.

we have demonstrated that FRS can be used for fast access control of a large number (thousands) of individuals, and the TBI camera can be used as the front end of an FRS for fast and reliable face recognition.
The main takeaway from our work is that
FRS can be made practical and reliable for ACS by using TBI and a one-to-one matching approach.
a fast and reliable FV solution can be achieved using a TBI camera with a unique face recognition (FR) algorithm that can handle a wide range of illumination, pose, and expression variations.
a FV system can be designed to be dynamic and reliable, and hence, can be used as part of an ACS system.
